why: MI-278 U29, RESEARCH lane. THREE lines in .gitattributes binding docs/claude/{performance,ml,research}-review-backlog.json to the EXISTING row-aware merge driver, plus a comment recording why, plus one backlog row. No code, no src/, no config/, no scripts/, no workflow, no order path. The driver itself (scripts/ops/merge_json_register.py) is UNCHANGED -- only which files git hands to it. WHY IT IS HELD RATHER THAN SELF-LANDING: .gitattributes is not in check_pr_landing's TIER1_SURFACE, and that allowlist is deliberately fail-closed -- an unrecognised path is one the guard cannot vouch for, not one that is thereby Tier-1. I am not claiming the guard is wrong; a file that changes how git MERGES every shared register is a reasonable thing for a human to read once, and it is exactly the class where a mistake is silent. THE EVIDENCE, MEASURED NOT ASSERTED: hand-resolving a conflict in performance-review-backlog.json on 2026-09-13 DROPPED a filed row that had landed on main hours earlier, and every check passed on the result -- backlog_refs, claim_basis, document-index, pr-landing and register-reserialization all green. Running merge_json_register.py over that conflict's exact three inputs (base 138 / ours 139 / theirs 139) exits 0 and returns the correct 140 with nothing dropped, so the driver was never the problem; the BINDING was missing. All four review backlogs share the shape the driver keys on (`items[]`, unique `id` on every row: 1566 / 139 / 111 / 19), so there is no shape reason only `health` was listed. Verified after the change with `git check-attr merge`: all four now resolve `jsonregister`, and the guard's own census moves 5 -> 8 bound, 23 -> 20 unmarked. WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: it does not bind the other 20 unmarked candidates. A row-aware driver pointed at a file that is not an id-keyed row register would be a new defect rather than a fix, and triaging them is named as the next step in the filed row instead of guessed at here. It also does not claim to make a `dirty` PR auto-mergeable -- the driver is client-side, as .gitattributes' own header already says.
hold_text: HELD ON PATH VOUCHABILITY, NOT ON DOUBT ABOUT THE CHANGE. .gitattributes is outside TIER1_SURFACE, so check_pr_landing cannot vouch for it and R-self-land correctly refuses; the allowlist is fail-closed by design and this is the case it is for. The change is three lines binding three files to a driver that already exists, is already installed in this clone, and is already bound to their sibling. WHAT A REVIEWER SHOULD CHECK, so the read is cheap: (a) that the three files really are id-keyed row registers -- `python3 -c` over each shows `items[]` with a unique `id` on every row; (b) that the driver handles them -- it is the same one health-review-backlog.json has used since it was bound; (c) that nothing else in .gitattributes moved -- the diff is an insertion after line 35 and touches no existing line. IT IS NOT URGENT IN THE SENSE OF A LIVE POSITION, and it is not cosmetic either: the incident that produced it silently deleted a filed backlog row on a branch while every guard read green, and the same hand-resolution happens on these files most days. If a reviewer prefers to bind only the performance backlog (the one with the measured incident) and leave ml and research for the triage step, that is a legitimate narrower call -- say so and I will cut it down rather than argue for the wider one.
